subject: Biology
title: Why Does Sex Exist?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Why Does Sex Exist?.

hook.text: Asexual reproduction is twice as efficient. So why do most complex organisms bother with sex?

buildup.text: Sexual reproduction costs energy, time, and requires finding a mate—a huge disadvantage.

discovery.text: Sex shuffles genes every generation, creating genetic diversity that helps resist parasites and disease.

twist.text: The Red Queen hypothesis says sex exists because parasites evolve so fast that clones can't keep up.

climax.text: Species that switch from sexual to asexual reproduction often go extinct within thousands of years.

punchline.text: Sex is expensive. But cloning is a death sentence.

quiz.question: According to the Red Queen hypothesis, why does sex exist?
options: To create genetic diversity that outpaces parasites

details.summary: Sexual reproduction is costly compared to asexual reproduction because only half of offspring are female, yet nearly all complex organisms reproduce sexually. The leading explanation is that sex creates genetic diversity that helps populations resist parasites and adapt to changing environments.
details.whyItMatters: The evolution of sex is called the queen of problems in evolutionary biology because its costs are so high. Understanding why sex persists despite these costs reveals fundamental truths about how evolution maintains adaptation.
takeaways: Sex has a twofold cost because males do not directly produce offspring
The Red Queen hypothesis argues sex provides defense against parasites
Genetic recombination during sex purges harmful mutations more efficiently

faq.question: What is the twofold cost of sex?
faq.answer: In an asexual population, every individual produces offspring. In a sexual population, only females produce offspring while males contribute only genes. An asexual mutant could theoretically double its population growth rate, yet sexual species persist, demanding explanation.

faq.question: Why not just reproduce asexually?
faq.answer: Asexual lineages accumulate harmful mutations with no way to purge them, called Muller's ratchet. They also cannot reshuffle genes to produce novel combinations for parasite defense. Most asexual lineages go extinct rapidly in evolutionary time for these reasons.
